title: I loved School Girls; Or, The African Mean Girls Play when I first sa...
transcript: in 2017 I saw School Girls or the African Mean Girls play off Broadway at that time in my life I hadn't seen a lot of plays and I was so blown away so when m t C announced that they were bringing School Girls to Broadway with Deneé Benton and Jasmine Rogers and Patina Miller obviously honestly I could not wait to see it again but I was so curious how this play would feel now and turns out it hit me even harder the second time schoolgirls takes us to an all girls boarding school in Ghana in 1986 it's kind of a reverse mean Queen Bee Paulina rules this school until Erica a new student from America shows up which causes big drama when they all enter a beauty pageant to become Miss Gone I love this show so much Whitney Waydes direction is exceptional and I am obsessed with the entire ensemble it's also ridiculous ridiculously funny and yet underneath all the jokes are these massively important conversations about western beauty standards and colourism and who gets to decide who is beautiful you start the play almost dismissing them because they are teenage girls and a beauty pageant feels like the kind of thing that is life or death when you're 16 years old but by the end you realise what these girls are fighting against is that serious they're not just squabbling over a beauty pageant they're struggling with a system that is designed to fail them they're just girls who want to feel worthy and who want to feel like they're enough school girls may take place in the 80s but the conversations are unfortunately still very relevant today you gotta see it
reasoning: Creator expresses strong enthusiasm throughout, praises direction and ensemble, highlights themes, and ends with explicit recommendation.
